correctness.rationale: The proof derives exact polygon area and Fock normalization, controls the perturbation by symmetric-difference area, preserves the disk top eigenvalue gap, identifies the first allowed cyclic coupling with coefficient \(-2e^{-A}A^{N/2+1}/(N^2\sqrt{N!})\), bounds the higher Fock tail, and computes the Schur resolvent on that mode. The leading factorial gain and eigenfunction coefficient follow. Symbolic integration verifies coefficients through \(h^8\); high-precision tests agree. All quantities are for fixed A>0, N tending to infinity.

originality.rationale: The disk extremality and general stability results do not determine the sharp \(N^{-4}\) polygon loss, the \((N!)^{-1}\) spectral optimization gain, or the first high-degree maximizing coefficient. The latter two require an exact rotational selection rule, factorial tail and Schur-complement limit. Search findings and directly inspected primary text support a provisional, not definitive, originality assessment.
residual_risks: An earlier Toeplitz or anti-Wick spectral approximation theorem could implicitly include the same regular-polygon coefficient.

value.rationale: Regular polygon observation masks are a canonical geometric approximation to the optimal disk. The exact \(N^{-4}\) loss and sharp factorial improvement from signal optimization separate two naturally different errors and quantify a high-order selection rule. This addresses a precise sharp asymptotic not settled by general disk optimality or stability exponents, with direct relevance to polygonal finite-aperture time-frequency design.
